cells.tense: This balance is holding now, and it holds because you keep adjusting the scale.
cells.ask: Name one exchange that is working, out loud, and say what makes it fair. Nothing else — just say it once.
cells.core:
You are in an exchange that runs both ways, and you keep it level without making a project of it. When something tips, you notice, you say so, and the two of you put it right. That ordinary maintenance is the whole of it. It does not look like much from inside.

It isn't a still point you found once and froze. It's a run of small corrections you keep making, and the corrections are what it is. What it's free to feed next is something bigger than the two of you — a third thing that can only be built on ground that holds. Keep the ground.
cells.sheetLine: You keep the give and take level, and you keep doing it.
cells.verb: recalibrating what has slipped between give and take
cells.place: where fairness is measured between people

cells.tense: You are already bracing for a reckoning that has not happened, and the bracing is the strain.
cells.ask: Let one imbalance stand uncorrected for a week. Do not name it, fix it, or log it. Just leave it.
cells.core:
You are tracking every exchange ahead of time, tallying what you have given and what might come back, and you are carrying the whole ledger like a load. From outside it looks like fairness. From inside it is a running audit you cannot put down. The system that was supposed to keep things even has become the thing that keeps you tense.

Fairness that has to be enforced stops being fair and turns into control. There is a shape where the scale settles by itself, because the people in it are decent. You have not tested that shape. You have only tested the one where you hold both ends.
cells.sheetLine: You are carrying the scale instead of letting it balance.
cells.verb: recalibrating what has slipped between give and take

cells.tense: You are still standing behind a door that closed, and you have not come in from it.
cells.ask: Set one small thing you are owed back on the table — a message, a favor returned, a yes to something offered. One.
cells.core:
In the good version you feel the small ones — what you owe, what's owed you — without keeping a book. You hand back what you borrowed, you say yes when you mean it, and the whole thing stays light because it moves. Nothing sits long enough to harden.

Something went out of balance and you stopped reaching for the scale. So you stepped back from exchanges altogether, and from that distance nothing looks giveable. The eye for it is not gone. It is unloaded, and you are waiting at a door that is already behind you.

The way back: notice what is owed and what you owe, in small precise amounts, until your eye for it returns. Fairness is a skill and you are out of shape, not broken. Start with an amount you can lift.
cells.sheetLine: You stopped keeping score, and now nothing feels owed either way.
cells.verb: recalibrating what has slipped between give and take
cells.place: where fairness is measured between people

cells.tense: You are already reading what is fair in a situation, and you are calling it something else.
cells.ask: Say one fairness judgment you have already made out loud, plainly, to the person it concerns.
cells.core:
You pick up when something between people is off. It arrives before anyone says it out loud, and the read tends to hold up. That reading is running now, shaping what you say yes to and what you quietly decline. You call it being realistic, or reading the room, or just not making a fuss.

The read is yours and it lands true, but you are not claiming it. So the adjustments you make go unexplained, and the people around you feel the shift without the reason. Saying it is not a confrontation. It is the same line, said once, where it can be heard.
cells.sheetLine: You spot what is fair before it is said. Say it once.
cells.verb: recalibrating what has slipped between give and take
cells.place: where fairness is measured between people
